title: Tech Note: Custom Values in the 4D Ajax Framework
author: Tim Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Chart, Grid, and Query custom value attachment

historical_commentary.text: Custom Values were a clever mechanism for passing arbitrary developer-defined parameters between the 4D Ajax Framework web frontend and the backend 4D database without relying on specific framework objects like Data Grids. Working with the beta-stage Data Bridge 2.0 object (successor to Bridge 1.0), developers could send custom values from JavaScript, intercept them in the DAX_DevHook_OnQuery backend method, and return computed results back to JavaScript—enabling scenarios like dynamic price calculation (the example uses a car dealership quoting system where model selection triggers custom value updates to recompute color/option prices). This pattern was foundational for 4DAF interactivity but became obsolete when 4D adopted REST APIs and ORDA, relegating Custom Values to a historical footnote in 4D's web architecture.
related_updates: 4D Ajax Framework and Data Bridge 2.0 have been discontinued
Custom Values as a data exchange mechanism have no direct equivalent in modern 4D
REST APIs (v12+) replaced the DAX hook/custom variable pattern with standard HTTP request/response
ORDA (v18+) and JSON provide native, type-safe data exchange without manual name/value pair marshaling
